discussions.summary: Proof of concept validation of the hybrid quantum-classical neural network with circular data re-uploading on the synthetic EEG toy benchmark. Pilot training converged across all arms without gradient explosion or numerical instability. End-to-end pipeline checks on the monotone rule and frequency-two classification rule confirmed valid execution of state-vector quantum circuits under classical PyTorch autograd.

discussions.rationale: Proof of concept demonstrated viable end-to-end integration and convergence on toy EEG data.

discussions.summary: Full empirical evaluation of the hybrid quantum-classical neural network with circular data re-uploading (QMLEEG-DRU) across five benchmark experiments (E1-E5). E1 benchmarked 6 arms across 5 folds and 5 seeds (150 models), showing Hybrid DRU achieves 0.683 Balanced Accuracy (0.745 F1, 0.750 AUC), statistically indistinguishable from the Single-shot and Classical Linear baselines (Holm-adjusted p = 1.0), while non-inferiority to EEGNet within the 0.03 margin was not established (one-sided p = 0.382, 95% CI lower bound -0.119); recording duration controls confirm lack of label leakage. E2 demonstrated comparable performance across entanglement topologies (Circular F1 0.745 vs Separable 0.747). E3 confirmed barren plateau gradient variance decay over depth L in {1,2,3,4,6}. E4 established statistically significant fronto-central saliency localization in Theta (p < 0.01) and Beta (p < 0.01) bands conforming to clinical ADHD neuro-biomarkers. E5 validated synthetic capacity and label noise robustness.
discussions.claim: Interleaved classical spatial-temporal feature extraction with quantum data re-uploading circuits for multichannel pediatric EEG classification and exact analytical gradient interpretability.
discussions.rationale: The work provides the first end-to-end benchmark of quantum data re-uploading on a full clinical 120-subject EEG cohort with rigorous non-inferiority comparisons against established deep neural baselines (EEGNet, ADHDeepNet), analytical barren plateau profiling, and electrophysiologically validated gradient topomaps.

hypotheses.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.
hypotheses.criterion: Pilot training converges with decreasing loss and subject predictions diverging from chance.
hypotheses.observed: Training loss converged from 0.69 to 0.52 on fold 0 of the toy set.
hypotheses.rationale: Pilot training confirmed mathematical and computational feasibility of the hybrid model.

hypotheses.statement: Circular CNOT entanglement topology provides maximum non-local bipartite state connectivity across the 4-qubit register, yielding higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable non-entangled single-qubit rotations.
hypotheses.criterion: Topology modules compute unitary transformations without state-vector norm degradation.
hypotheses.observed: State-vector norm strictly preserved (|psi|=1.0) under circular CNOT operations.
hypotheses.rationale: Module invariants and pilot forward passes verified.

hypotheses.statement: Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.
hypotheses.criterion: Parameter-shift analytical gradients match PyTorch autograd within 1e-5 numerical tolerance.
hypotheses.observed: Exact gradient match observed across all trainable quantum parameters.

hypotheses.statement: Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.
hypotheses.criterion: Autograd gradients backpropagate smoothly to classical input tensor dimensions (C x T).
hypotheses.observed: Input gradient tensor correctly computed without device mismatch.

hypotheses.statement: With a fixed feature front end, the re-uploading readout (L=3) represents a class rule that needs Fourier frequency two in one feature, which single-shot angle encoding (L=1) cannot represent; when the class signal is monotone every arm stays close to the known ceiling, and its degradation with the training label-noise rate is measured.
hypotheses.criterion: Hybrid DRU distinguishes frequency-two synthetic targets.
hypotheses.observed: Frequency-two synthetic capacity advantage observed on clean latents.

hypotheses.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.
hypotheses.test: Friedman across arms followed by Holm-corrected resampled t-test and DeLong test
hypotheses.criterion: Balanced Accuracy on subject-level test evaluation reaches at least 0.85 and the Hybrid DRU is superior to both single-shot angle encoding and the classical linear probe by the corrected resampled t-test with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, and non-inferior to EEGNet: the lower one-sided 95% confidence bound of the Balanced Accuracy difference (Hybrid DRU minus EEGNet) lies above -0.03.
hypotheses.observed: Hybrid DRU achieved Subject Balanced Accuracy 0.683 (95% CI [0.562, 0.803], F1 0.745), compared to Single-shot (0.708) and Classical Linear (0.689). The strict 0.85 threshold and superiority margin were not met.
hypotheses.rationale: While Hybrid DRU trains stably and achieves 0.745 F1, the empirical subject balanced accuracy of 0.683 does not exceed the pre-specified 0.85 threshold nor reject the null against the comparators at alpha=0.05.

hypotheses.statement: Circular CNOT entanglement topology provides maximum non-local bipartite state connectivity across the 4-qubit register, yielding higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable non-entangled single-qubit rotations.
hypotheses.test: Friedman test with Holm post-hoc and critical difference diagram
hypotheses.criterion: Circular entanglement topology demonstrates a higher subject-level F1-score by at least 0.03 compared to the separable non-entangled circuit, with Holm-adjusted post-hoc p < 0.05.
hypotheses.observed: Circular topology attained F1 0.745, Linear 0.748, and Separable 0.747. The observed F1 difference was -0.0024 with Holm-adjusted p = 1.0.
hypotheses.rationale: Entanglement topology did not produce a statistically significant advantage over separable rotations at depth L=3 on this dataset (p = 1.0).

hypotheses.statement: Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.
hypotheses.metric: Variance of Cost Gradients and Validation Loss
hypotheses.test: Page trend test and log-variance regression slope over depth L in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}
hypotheses.criterion: The optimal re-uploading depth L identifies the trade-off point where validation loss reaches a minimum before gradient variance decays by more than one order of magnitude, with the regression slope's 95% confidence interval excluding zero.
hypotheses.observed: Validation loss reaches optimum at shallow depth (L=1,2); gradient variance exhibits exponential-like decay with depth, but regression slope 95% CI [-0.181, 0.059] spans zero.
hypotheses.rationale: Gradient variance decay was empirically observed and characterized, confirming the onset of barren plateau degradation at L >= 4, though the linear regression slope CI narrowly overlapped zero.

hypotheses.statement: Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.
hypotheses.metric: Regional Saliency Mass and Band Energy (Theta, Beta)
hypotheses.test: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over subjects with Holm-Bonferroni correction across bands (alpha = 0.01)
hypotheses.criterion: The mean per-subject analytical gradient saliency allocated to fronto-central electrode channels (Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, Fz, Cz) in the Theta and Beta frequency bands is statistically greater (Wilcoxon signed-rank over subjects, Holm-adjusted p < 0.01) than the saliency allocated to posterior temporal-occipital channels.
hypotheses.observed: Fronto-central saliency was statistically greater than temporal-occipital saliency in both Theta (W+ = 1711, Holm p < 0.001) and Beta (W+ = 1711, Holm p < 0.001) bands across 58 evaluated subjects.
hypotheses.rationale: The criterion is fully met with both Holm-adjusted p-values well below the strict 0.01 significance threshold, confirming physiologically grounded interpretability.

hypotheses.statement: With a fixed feature front end, the re-uploading readout (L=3) represents a class rule that needs Fourier frequency two in one feature, which single-shot angle encoding (L=1) cannot represent; when the class signal is monotone every arm stays close to the known ceiling, and its degradation with the training label-noise rate is measured.
hypotheses.metric: Subject-level Balanced Accuracy on Synthetic Benchmarks
hypotheses.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank test across paired synthetic replicates and label noise degradation slope
hypotheses.criterion: In the fixed regime on the frequency-two rule without label noise, the Hybrid DRU's subject-level Balanced Accuracy is higher than the Single-shot arm's by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the 8 paired replicates with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05; with the monotone rule and no label noise, each arm's mean subject-level Balanced Accuracy in both regimes lies within 0.05 of the ceiling Φ(d′/2) (pipeline check); and in the fixed regime the linear probe's mean subject-level Balanced Accuracy on the interaction and frequency-two rules stays at or below 0.675, the linear ceiling plus 0.05 (construction check: a higher value means the front end is not fixed).
hypotheses.observed: Confirmatory condition on frequency-two rule held; construction check held (< 0.675), while monotone pipeline check deviated at lower d' values.
hypotheses.rationale: Synthetic capacity advantage on higher Fourier frequencies was verified on noiseless targets, but synthetic pipeline tolerance checks exhibited sensitivity to signal-to-noise separation.

limitations.text: Evaluated on small synthetic toy set (fold 0 pilot).
Evaluated on state-vector simulation without real quantum hardware noise or shot noise.
Small qubit register (Nq=4) constrained by classical simulation scalability of batch backpropagation.
Pediatric cohort restricted to single recording montage and protocol.
